account: A 34-year-old man of Egyptian origin began a dialogue with the DeepSeek-R1-0528 model on 28 June 2025. He had recurrent fever, migratory abdominal pain, arthralgia, myalgia and erythematous skin lesions since early childhood. The model refined its differential toward familial Mediterranean fever (FMF). It recommended specialist evaluation, inflammatory markers, genetic testing and colchicine under supervision. He arranged genetic testing, which found two pathogenic MEFV variants (p.Met694Val and p.Val726Ala). He obtained colchicine 0.5 mg twice daily from an Egyptian pharmacy. His attacks ceased, but alanine aminotransferase rose to 160 U/L. Colchicine was temporarily discontinued, and his primary care physician monitored his liver enzymes. After they improved, colchicine was resumed at 0.5 mg daily under close supervision. In February 2026 he presented to the Department of Medicine III, University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf, Germany, already taking 0.5 mg daily. The clinic confirmed FMF, and he has remained attack-free. The authors of the case report declare that they have no competing interests. In a study published on 31 October 2025, Selin Cilli Hayıroğlu and Tugce Bozkurt, rheumatologists in Istanbul, found that ChatGPT, Gemini and Grok answered diagnosis questions on FMF less well than other questions about the disease.

ai_role.statement: The large language model (LLM) generated the FMF hypothesis and the suggested work-up over a multi-turn dialogue. Confirmation came from MEFV genotyping and clinical response to colchicine. The authors stress that the model repeatedly advised specialist supervision. The self-directed genetic testing and self-medication were the patient's own actions.

He arranged genetic testing, which found two pathogenic MEFV variants (p.Met694Val and p.Val726Ala). He obtained colchicine 0.5 mg twice daily from an Egyptian pharmacy. His attacks ceased, but alanine aminotransferase rose to 160 U/L. Colchicine was temporarily discontinued, and his primary care physician monitored his liver enzymes. After they improved, colchicine was resumed at 0.5 mg daily under close supervision. In February 2026 he presented to the Department of Medicine III, University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf, Germany, already taking 0.5 mg daily. The clinic confirmed FMF, and he has remained attack-free. The authors of the case report declare that they have no competing interests. In a study published on 31 October 2025, Selin Cilli Hayıroğlu and Tugce Bozkurt, rheumatologists in Istanbul, found that ChatGPT, Gemini and Grok answered diagnosis questions on FMF less well than other questions about the disease.
